title: Emit calls from typed function-pointer signatures
goal: Generate an indirect call from an actual managed or unmanaged function-pointer Type; use for trusted runtime adapters when dynamic code is supported and the target ABI and lifetime are known.

sdk.reason: Build against .NET 11 references; exact RC2 pins record measured artifacts.
sdk.name: .NET SDK

language.reason: Canonical declared language mode; no preview syntax switch.
language.name: C#

packageAssets: Framework reference/runtime assemblies; no NuGet package route.
prerequisites: Console net11.0 project with nullable/implicit usings and AllowUnsafeBlocks=true.
RuntimeFeature.IsDynamicCodeSupported must be true before DynamicMethod creation.
Known valid managed/native function-pointer signatures and addresses; keep native library alive through invocation.
platforms: Windows x64 CoreCLR with system kernel32 MulDiv export; no x86/Arm/Mono/browser/WASI execution proof.
stabilityLimitations: Actual RC2 verification, not final-GA proof; PIN-962 and PIN-959 remain open.
constraints: Requires runtime code generation and trusted IL inputs; no Native AOT execution route.
Exact function-pointer ABI, stack order and live address/library ownership remain caller obligations.
Windows MulDiv consumer only. x64 unified ABI does not distinguish x86 calling conventions; no implicit marshalling or last-error preservation.
